verdict.summary: Composio has no managed Shopify app, so you must register your own. Custom distribution (one store or one Plus org) needs no review. Installing on many stores needs public distribution and App Store review, and Shopify publishes no turnaround.
verdict.hands_on_effort: 1-2 hours for your own store; days to weeks for App Store submission
verdict.approval_wait: None for custom distribution; about 1-2 weeks per review cycle for public (community-reported, not official)

gates.name: Custom distribution / development store
gates.unlocks: Install on your own store, stores in one Plus organization, or development stores
limits: Custom distribution cannot be changed after selection
Single store or one Plus organization only
Creating one custom app per merchant to avoid review is not allowed unless the apps are unique per merchant (community answer)
New custom apps can't be created in the Shopify admin after Jan 1, 2026; use the Dev Dashboard

gates.name: Public distribution in Draft / limited visibility listing
gates.unlocks: Development-store installs; limited-visibility public apps go through the same review
limits: Community reports production-store installs are blocked until the app is reviewed, while development stores work
Limited-visibility public apps have the same requirements as fully visible ones
No numeric install cap was found in official docs
If an unreviewed app can be installed by other stores, your app must enforce which stores may install it (community report)
gates.time_to_reach: Same day for dev stores; review needed for production stores

gates.name: Public app on the Shopify App Store
limits: Failing core requirements moves the app to Paused; fix and use Submit fixes
Protected customer data (level 1 and 2) requires review for public apps
Approval-labelled scopes need Shopify approval via Support
Revenue share is 0% on the first $1M lifetime, then 15%
App Store registration has a one-time fee
gates.time_to_reach: Days to weeks after submission; no official turnaround

steps.title: Choose a distribution method
steps.detail: Decide between custom distribution (one store or one Plus org, no review) and public distribution (many stores, review). You can't change this after selecting, so decide before creating the app.
gotchas: Public distribution also requires registering for the Shopify App Store
Composio-style 'enter your store URL' connect flows conflict with App Store rules for public apps

steps.title: Create the app in the Dev Dashboard
steps.detail: Sign in to the Dev Dashboard and create a new app. The admin-based custom app type is no longer available for new apps.
gotchas: The probe got HTTP 406 for this URL, and account prerequisites were not confirmed

steps.title: Set redirect URL and scopes
steps.detail: Add the redirect URL and access scopes in the app configuration. A tutorial says these are declared in shopify.app.toml and registered with shopify app deploy. Trim Composio's broad default scope list to what you need, because a write scope also grants read.

values.label: Redirect URI
values.value: Composio callback URL (see the Composio callout on this page)

gotchas: Any redirect_uri sent in the authorize request must match the host of the configured callback URL

steps.title: Copy client ID and secret into Composio
steps.detail: Create a Shopify auth config in Composio with your app's client_id and client_secret. Authorization and token URLs are templated per store ({subdomain}.myshopify.com), so supply your shop domain when connecting.

steps.title: Install and connect your own store
steps.detail: Install the app on your store or a development store and run the Composio connect flow. Confirm the grant screen shows the requested scopes and the token exchange succeeds.
gotchas: The authorize URL doesn't reject unknown client_ids, so a successful page load doesn't prove your client_id is right

steps.title: Request approval for restricted scopes
steps.detail: If you use scopes labelled 'Shopify approval required' (e.g. read_shopify_payments, read_all_orders-type scopes), request approval through Shopify Support. Request only what the app needs, since Shopify may ask for proof.
gotchas: Many Composio default scopes were not checked for approval gating

steps.title: Request protected customer data access
steps.detail: In the Partner Dashboard go to Apps, open API access requests, click Request access on Protected customer data, select fields, complete Data protection details and submit. Level 2 fields (name, email, phone, address) are requested individually. Development-store-only apps can skip review.
gotchas: Without approval the API won't return data from non-development stores
Shopify may request a detailed data protection review

steps.title: Prepare App Store submission materials
steps.detail: Draft the listing, a unique app name matching the Dev Dashboard config, and scope justifications. Check the app against requirements: GraphQL Admin API only, valid TLS, OAuth immediately after install, no manual myshopify.com entry, and Shopify Billing for charges.
gotchas: Off-platform billing is not allowed on the App Store

steps.title: Record screencast, set up test credentials and emergency contact
steps.detail: Record an English (or subtitled) demo of onboarding and features. Provide working test credentials with full feature access and set an emergency developer contact in the Partner Dashboard.

steps.title: Submit for review and wait
steps.detail: Submit the app for review. If it moves to Paused, follow the emailed changes and use Submit fixes. No official turnaround was found; community reports are 5-10 business days or 1-2 weeks per cycle.

requirements.detail: Required before creating the app and before requesting protected customer data; can't be changed later.
New public apps since April 1, 2025 must use the GraphQL Admin API exclusively.

requirements.item: OAuth immediately after install; no manual shop domain entry
requirements.detail: Public apps must authenticate with OAuth first and must not ask for a myshopify.com URL.
Request only needed scopes, use optional scopes for non-universal needs, and be ready to prove the need.

requirements.item: Valid TLS and no critical errors
requirements.detail: Valid TLS certificate and no 404/500 errors that block review.
Charges must go through Shopify App Pricing or Billing API.
Level 1 has nine requirements (including minimum data, consent, retention and encryption). Level 2 adds backups, access logs, incident response and more.

scopes.scope: read_shopify_payments / read_payment_gateways / read_customer_payment_methods (and other approval-labelled scopes)
scopes.effect: Shopify must approve the app before you can declare the scope; request through Shopify Support.
Protected customer data. Public apps need review; non-development stores return no data until approved.
Also grant read access. Request only if both are needed.

blockers.symptom: Install on a production store is blocked with a message that the app needs to be reviewed
blockers.cause: The app uses public distribution and has not been approved (community report); development stores work.
blockers.fix: Submit for App Store review, or switch to custom distribution if you need only one store or one Plus org. The distribution method can't be changed on an existing app, so create a new app.

blockers.symptom: API returns redacted or no customer data on real stores
blockers.cause: The app isn't approved for protected customer data.
blockers.fix: Request protected customer data access and the individual level 2 fields in the Partner Dashboard.

blockers.symptom: App moved to Paused after submission
blockers.fix: Read the email, fix the listed issues and click Submit fixes.

blockers.cause: The scope carries a Shopify approval label.

composio.note: No managed OAuth app exists for Shopify, so you must register your own app from the start. For your own store use custom distribution. A public listed app can't ask merchants to type a myshopify.com domain, which conflicts with Composio's per-store connect step. Composio's default scope list is broad, so trim it. The list shown here is abbreviated.

open_questions: No official install cap for unlisted or unreviewed public apps was found.
Official review turnaround is not stated; 5-10 business days and 1-2 weeks are community figures.
Expiring offline token dates (new public apps; existing apps before Jan 1, 2027) come from third-party blogs only.
Whether unlisted public apps need full review rests on community answers.
Developer account prerequisites (Partner account, org role, fees) were not confirmed; the Dev Dashboard probe returned 406.
The Common review problems page and the full requirements list were not reviewed.
Which Composio default scopes are approval-gated was not checked.
